title: 如何借助统一访问策略简化云访问（预览版）
author: Siddharth Deekshit, Prateek Jain
content:
As organizations scale their cloud footprint to thousands of autonomous agents and microservices, you can accidentally create an operational bottleneck with strict Identity and Access Management (IAM). Meanwhile, administrators still need to enforce least privilege across thousands of resources without slowing down engineering velocity.

Enter Unified Access Policies (UAPs), Google Cloud's next-generation access control engine in Cloud IAM, now in preview at no additional cost. UAP consolidates allow and deny rules into one unified schema, and decouples policy definition from resource enforcement. 

This approach allows you to author a policy once and bind it across your organization. UAP governs human, workload, and first-class agent identities with your existing IAM policies. With UAP, you can radically simplify your access policies and manage them more easily at scale.

Scale limitations of legacy access models

Traditional access policy models can push teams into a tough trade-off between Zero Trust access and pipeline speed due to three compounding forces:

  1. Fragmented schemas and permission sprawl: In granting thousands of granular permissions across cloud resources, administrators are forced to choose between either over-granting permissions from coarse roles with broad access, or wrangling two different syntaxes (APIs and mental models across allow and deny) just to define one workload's custom access posture.

  2. Policies treated as snowflakes: Because legacy policies attach directly to individual resources, applying a standard developer or security baseline across 25 projects means duplicating and maintaining 50 separate allow and deny policy configurations in Terraform. This approach can create severe configuration fatigue and operational burden, with greater risk of misconfiguration.

  3. Scale ceilings and explosion of agent identities: Modern cloud environments span human teams, federated workloads, service accounts, and autonomous agents that should never share generic service account credentials. As non-human and agent identities multiply, large enterprises routinely hit the hard 64 KB single-policy size limit on allow policies — requiring policy refactoring to onboard new teams or agents.

Helping platform and security teams address these access limitations demands a new approach: an agent-ready engine on a unified control plane, designed to simplify, centralize, and scale access control.

Key capabilities in UAP preview

UAP removes cognitive burden for platform and IAM administrators, security architects, and agent administrators while shrinking your Infrastructure as Code footprint. UAP re-architects how policies are authored, bound, and enforced across your resource hierarchy because it’s built around a simpler authorization model.

1. Unified allow and deny syntax: Consolidate positive access grants and firm security guardrails into a single, auditable policy instead of reconciling separate allow and deny files.

2. Multi-binding support: A standalone policy binding acts as the connective tissue between your policy definition and target Cloud Resource Manager (CRM) nodes (organization, folder, and project). You can now bind a single UAP policy across up to 25 CRM targets in preview, eliminating duplicate Terraform blocks.

3. Expanded scale limits (5x effective policy size): UAP breaks through the legacy single-policy size ceiling by letting you attach up to five UAP policies (64 KB and up to 100 rules each) to any single CRM resource — scaling to 2,500 unique principals and 500 groups per resource.

4. Clear separation of concerns: Central security architects can author vetted baseline and guardrail policies at the organization node and delegate self-service binding to folder and project administrators, without letting local teams alter central rule logic.

5. Expressive permission wildcards and immutable guardrails: Replace brittle permission lists with prefix, suffix, and substring wildcards alongside predefined roles and action exclusions (excluded permissions).

6. Built-in readiness for agents: UAP treats agents as first-class principals (principal://agents.global...) rather than generic service accounts. Agent administrators can scope least-privilege allow and deny rules directly to individual agents or entire agent pools, combine UAP with short-lived, downscoped tokens, and build on an extensible foundation for human-in-the-loop and delegated agent authorization.

7. Day 1 parity across all four surfaces: At runtime, Cloud IAM evaluates your existing allow policies, deny policies and UAP policies concurrently across your resource hierarchy. Whether your teams prefer interactive workflows or declarative automation, UAP launches with full create, read, update, and delete parity across the Google Cloud console, gCloud CLI, Terraform, and the Cloud IAM v3 REST API.

You can deploy your first policy to bring these powerful capabilities into your environment in just a few minutes.

Enforce UAP in 3 steps

While you can automate UAP through Terraform, gCloud CLI or REST API, you can also author and bind policies interactively in the Google Cloud console.

Step 1: Open the Unified Access Policies tab
In the Google Cloud console, select your target organization, folder, or project in the resource picker and navigate to IAM & Admin > IAM. 

Alongside the existing Principals tab, select the new Unified Access Policies tab to view all policies in your scope — including their binding status, governed principals and rule types — and click + Create policy.

Unified Access Policies page lists all the policies managed at/ enforced at the scope picked by the customer (Project, Folder or Org).

Step 2: Define policy details and access rules
In the Policy Details pane, enter a policy name and description, then build your access posture under Add rules:

  1. Select principals and exceptions: Choose a principal set or individual identity (such as dev group or agent identity) via + Add principal, and optionally exempt breakglass administrator groups via + Add exception principal.

  2. Choose the rule effect and permissions: Select Allow (using predefined roles, individual permissions or permission wildcards) or Deny (using explicit permissions or wildcards, such as compute.googleapis.com/firewalls.*)

  3. Combine rules in one policy: Click Add another rule to pair positive grants and deny guardrails in the same policy, while inspecting the live JSON configuration preview on the right.

Create Allow and/or Deny rules within a single UAP policy resource.

Step 3: Bind the policy and manage lifecycle
Proceed to the Enforcement step, select the target organization, folder, or project scopes where you want the policy to take effect, and click Bind policy. 

Once created, you can click any policy on the Unified Access Policies landing page to open its Policy details view — where you can audit active rules and resource bindings, click View JSON to export the policy for IaC pipelines, or edit bindings as your environment evolves.

Every policy can be bound to a target resource through a binding. Leveraging separate bindings, a single policy can be enforced on multiple resources, unlocking simpler management at scale.

With your first policy securely enforced and managed, your security and platform teams can spend less time wrangling permission sprawl and more time driving business velocity.

Get started today

With Unified Access Policies, we are excited to help you build a more secure, agile and future-ready cloud architecture that scales alongside your human and AI workloads.

To streamline your organization’s access management, explore the Unified Access Policies documentation, and try it in a test project — create and bind your first reusable UAP policy using gcloud CLI, REST API, or Terraform.
aiSummary: 统一访问策略（UAP）将允许和拒绝规则整合到统一架构中，从而在 Google Cloud 资源层级中，为数千个人员、工作负载和智能体身份提供集中且可扩展的访问控制。
oneSentenceSummary: 统一访问策略（UAP）将允许和拒绝规则整合到统一架构中，从而在 Google Cloud 资源层级中，为数千个人员、工作负载和智能体身份提供集中且可扩展的访问控制。
summary: 统一访问策略（UAP）是 Google Cloud 正处于预览阶段的新一代访问控制引擎，旨在解决传统 IAM 在管理云资源上数千条细粒度权限时面临的运营瓶颈。UAP 将允许和拒绝规则整合到统一架构中，将策略定义与资源强制执行分离，并将智能体视为一等主体。它支持最多跨 25 个 CRM 目标进行多重绑定，将每个资源的有效策略规模扩展至 2，500 个主体和 500 个群组，并明确区分安全架构师与本地管理员的职责。该系统帮助平台和安全团队简化访问策略、减少配置负担，并更轻松地大规模管理访问，同时确保贯彻最小权限原则。

mainPoints.point: UAP 将允许和拒绝规则整合到统一架构中
mainPoints.explanation: 传统 IAM 要求使用不同语法分别管理允许和拒绝策略，增加了认知负担。UAP 将两者整合到一个可审计的策略结构中，从而简化管理。

mainPoints.point: 支持多重绑定，可在 25 个 CRM 目标间复用策略
mainPoints.explanation: UAP 策略无需在各个资源上重复配置，而是可以绑定到多个组织、文件夹和项目节点，从而减少 Terraform 配置开销和运营负担。

mainPoints.point: 扩展后的规模上限可满足不断增长的智能体身份需求
mainPoints.explanation: UAP 突破了传统的单策略 64 KB 限制，允许每个资源最多配置 5 个策略，支持扩展至 2，500 个唯一主体和 500 个群组，以应对现代云环境中非人类身份和智能体身份不断增加的情况。

mainPoints.point: 内置支持将智能体视为一等主体
mainPoints.explanation: UAP 将智能体视为一等主体（principal://agents.global...），而非通用服务账号，使智能体管理员能够直接针对单个智能体或智能体池设定最小权限规则，并使用短期、权限范围受限的令牌。

mainPoints.point: 明确区分安全架构师与管理员的职责
mainPoints.explanation: 中央安全架构师可以在组织节点制定经过审核的基线策略，同时将绑定操作授权给文件夹和项目管理员自助完成，避免本地团队更改中央规则逻辑。

keyQuotes: UAP 将允许和拒绝规则整合到统一架构中，并将策略定义与资源强制执行分离
现在，你可以在预览版中将单个 UAP 策略绑定到最多 25 个 CRM 目标，从而消除重复的 Terraform 配置块
UAP 突破了传统的单策略大小上限：你可以为任何单个 CRM 资源关联最多 5 个 UAP 策略（每个策略为 64 KB，最多包含 100 条规则）
UAP 将智能体视为一等主体（principal://agents.global...），而非通用服务账号
借助 UAP，你可以大幅简化访问策略，并更轻松地大规模管理它们
